{{nihongo|'''Tarumi Shrine'''|垂水神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

'''Tarumi Shrine'' (Tarumi Shrine) is located in {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Suita|Q653510|qid=Q653510}}{{ill|Tarumi Town|Q136088206|qid=Q136088206|lt=Tarumi Town}}. It is {{ill|Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikiuchi|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}}), and {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=Old shrine rank}} is {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}. Currently {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Independent Shrine}} which does not belong to {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}<ref>Osaka Prefectural Shrine and Shrine Agency website [https://www.osaka-jinjacho.jp/funai_jinja/dai2shibu/suita-city/suita.html]</ref>.

==Enshrined God==
The following three deities are enshrined. </ref>.

In "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}}, which was established in 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), there is one enshrined deity. In the special ``Engishiki'' festival, there will be one troupe for the prayer rain god festival and the Meishin festival, but there will be two za for the Yasojima festival.

== About the enshrined deity ==
``Tarumi'' in the company name of Tarumi Shrine means ``water flowing down a cliff'' {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikinai Shrine)|1977}}. {{ill|Senri Hills|Q11406845|qid=Q11406845}}The precincts located at the southern end are topographically located where spring water comes from the hills, and Tarumi-jin, who is enshrined here, has been worshiped as the god of water since ancient times {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikiuchi-sha)|1977}}. As mentioned below, in the literature, ``{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}'' records the history of our company related to the water of ``Tarumi Oka'', and also {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=Kokokushi}} records that the imperial court made offerings to the shrine many times to pray for rain {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}. {{ill|Early modern period|Q5308718|qid=Q5308718}}'s ``{{ill|Settsu Meisho Zue|Q11498549|qid=Q11498549}}'' and ``Settsushi'' also contain descriptions of the spring water in this area, and in particular, ``Settsu Famous Places Zue'' describes how it was worshiped as a spiritual spring {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1977}}.In addition, in the Tarumi area, the ``Tarumi clan'' (Tarumi Uji, Tarumi ko) lived as an ancient clan, and it is known that they were involved in the rituals at Tarumi Shrine. Regarding this Tarumi clan, "Newly Selected Names and Names Roku" by Ukyo Emperor In Tarumi Kojo, he was named as a descendant of Kamo no Shinchi-no-Mikoto (the fourth-generation grandchild of Toyoki Irihiko-no-Mikoto), and in his dispensation, he was given the surname of ``Tarumi-ko'' at the time of Arima no Kimi (the sixth-generation grandson of Toyoki Irihiko-no-Mikoto), and the festival was held at Tarumi Shrine. He is said to have been in charge of the shrine. Toyoki Irihiko-no-Mikoto, who is considered a personal deity at the current Tarumi Shrine, is the distant ancestor of the Tarumi clan. One theory is that before the involvement of the Tarumi clan, the shrine had been enshrined as a simple shrine dedicated to the god of water, but it is also speculated that due to the involvement of the Tarumi clan, Toyogi Irihiko no Mikoto was appointed as the personal deity {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Gods)|2000}}. In addition, in the "Newly Selected Names and Names and Records", there is also a record of the history of Tarumi whose ancestor was Irihiko Toyoshiro no Mikoto by Sakyo-no-no-no-Ko.{{Sfn|Tarumi clan (Ancient clan names dictionary)|2010}}{{Sfn|Tarumi (Ancient clan dictionary)|2015}}.In the early modern "Settsu Famous Places Zue," the deity enshrined at the time was Toyogi Irihiko-no-Mikoto, and another theory states that the deity enshrined was {{ill|Hitachi Province|Q1055353|qid=Q1055353}} Yakushi Shrine (currently {{ill|Oarai Isosaki Shrine|Q11437230|qid=Q11437230}}), and there is also a theory that they are Ōki Takamiko and Sukunahikona no Mikoto {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}, and the current Tarumi Shrine enshrines all three of these deities. Also, {{ill|Ban Nobutomo|Q4346747|qid=Q4346747}} writes in ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|ar|نيهون شوكي|as|নিহন শ্ব'কি|az|Nihon şoki|bcl|Nihon Shoki|bg|Нихоншоки|ca|Nihon Shoki|cs|Nihonšoki|de|Nihonshoki|el|Νιχόν Σόκι|eo|Nihon Ŝoki|es|Nihonshoki|eu|Nihon Shoki|fa|نیهون شوکی|fi|Nihonshoki|fr|Nihon shoki|gl|Nihon Shoki|he|ניהון שוקי|hi|निहोन शोकी|hr|Nihon Shoki|hu|Nihonsoki|id|Nihon Shoki|it|Nihon shoki|ja|日本書紀|jv|Nihon Shoki|ko|일본서기|la|Nihon Shoki|mk|Нихон шоки|ms|Nihon Shoki|my|နိဟွန်းရှောခိ|nl|Nihon Shoki|no|Nihonshoki|oc|Nihon shoki|pl|Nihon-shoki|pt|Nihon Shoki|rsk|Нихон Шоки|ru|Нихон сёки|sco|Nihon Shoki|sh|Nihon Shoki|simple|Nihon Shoki|sl|Nihon Šoki|sq|Nihon Shoki|sr|Нихон шоки|sv|Nihonshoki|ta|நிஹான் ஷோகி|th|นิฮงโชกิ|tl|Nihon Shoki|tr|Nihon Shoki|uk|Ніхон Сьокі|uz|Nihon shoki|vi|Nhật Bản thư kỷ|zh|日本書紀|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Su-kì|zh_yue|日本書紀|qid=Q813935}}'' in ``{{ill|Jinmyōchō Kōshō Dodai|Q11588823|qid=Q11588823}}''. {jalink|Empress Jingu|Q232803}} The theory is that the enshrined deity is {{ill|Yosami no Otarumi|Q24899491|qid=Q24899491}}, which appears in the {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}.

== History ==

== Founding ==
The date of its construction is unknown {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1977}}. "{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}" Ukyo no Betsu According to Tarumi Kojo, the time of {{ill|Emperor Kōtoku|Q317980|qid=Q317980}} ({{ill|645|Q31040|qid=Q31040}}-{{jalink |654|Q31109}}), there was a drought, but Prince Arima (grandchild of Toyogi Irihiko no Mikoto VI) traveled from Tarumi-oka to Takahi to visit the Emperor's Palace ({{ill|Tarumi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|qid=Tarumi Shrine (Shikinaisha)|lt=1977}}{{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}{{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Gods)|2000}}.

It is located in the center of the Tarumi ruins and Tarumi Minami ruins, which are thought to be the core settlements of the Yayoi period.

In the group="Hara" name="New Year's Day of the First Year of Jogan"/>, you can see an article about promotion to Junior Fourth Rank Lower {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.{{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Extension}} 5 years ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}) "{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}" {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shinmyocho}} Settsu Province {{ill|Teshima district|Q11633558|qid=Q11633558|lt=Toshima District}} "Tarumi Shrine Meishin University It is listed in {{ill|Myōjin Taisha|Q9610964|qid=Q9610964}} as the ``Monthly Niiname Shrine,'' and it is also stated that it is entrusted to the Imperial Court's {{ill|Tsukinami-no-Matsuri|Q11516161|qid=Q11516161}} and {{ill|Niiname-no-Matsuri|Q11501518|qid=Q11501518}} {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Also, in the special ``Engishiki'' festival, Tarumi is mentioned among the gods who receive medals at the {{ill|Yasojima Festival|Q24870749|qid=Q24870749|lt=Yasoshima God Festival}}, Prayer God Festival, and Meishin Festival {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. Among the place names that appear in the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542|lt=Japanese Namesho}} from the middle of the {{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}}, this place is identified as Toshima-go, Toshima District.{{ill|Hōan|Q1194464|qid=Q1194464|lt=Security}} In the first year of the year ({{ill|1120|Q19542|qid=Q19542}}), the "Settsu Province Tax Book Draft" describes Kobe, the god of Tarumi, as "Tarumi Kobe Ichie". In addition to the "Annual Tribute Order for Jingikan Shrines" in the first year of {{ill|Eiman|Q1193868|qid=Q1193868}} ({{ill|1165|Q19676|qid=Q19676}}) and the fifth year of {{ill|Bunji (era)|Q1194415|qid=Q1194415}} ({{ill|1189|Q19735|qid=Q19735}}) Kasugasha Ryo Tarumi Nishimaki Enokizaka Goda Hatatoricho, {{ill|Jōji|Q1146153|qid=Q1146153}}5 ({{ill|1366|Q6194|qid=Q6194}})'s ``Kasugasha Ryō Tarumi Nishimaki Enokizakagouchi Toho Catalog'' also mentions Tarumi Shrine {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

The changes during the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} period are not clear because there are almost no descriptions in historical materials{{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}. According to the shrine's legend, it declined due to military fire {{Sfn|Tarumi Shrine (Heibonsha)|1986}}.

{{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, {{ill|Tenna|Q1145289|qid=Q1145289|lt=Tenwa}} In the 3rd year ({{ill|1683|Q7651|qid=Q7651}}), the shrine building was rebuilt.After {{ill|Meiji Restoration|Q8707|qid=Q8707}}, in {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}5 ({{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}}), {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}} It was listed as a {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and in February 1907 (Meiji 40|1907|Q2048}}, it was designated as a Shinto shrine). Later, in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}}49 ({{ill|1974|Q2478|qid=Q2478}}), the shrine building you see today was rebuilt.

== Modern ==
{{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}In April 2013, a briefing session was held for nearby residents about the plan to demolish Tarumi Shrine's "Chinju no Mori" to develop condominiums.<ref>Yomiuri Shimbun (Osaka Morning Edition), December 18, 2013, p. </ref>. Parishioners who learned about the condominium development at an information session formed the Tarumi Forest Protection Association and began opposing the project. Around 100 banners were erected around the shrine protesting against the construction of condominiums, posters opposing the construction were put up, and approximately 13,000 people submitted signatures opposing Suita City, which had granted the development permit. They also discovered that construction of condominiums would require roads on land owned by a shrine, and refused construction vehicles access, forcing the development to be halted. <ref> Asahi Shimbun (Osaka morning edition), January 11, 2014, p. 33. </ref>.

{{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} In February 2015, a condominium developer approached the shrine about purchasing the planned land, and in November of the same year, the shrine collected donations and purchased the land, and a contract was concluded, thus preserving the ``Chinju-no-Mori.'' According to Itoya, director of the NPO Shaso Gakkai, even if compromises such as revising plans are sometimes passed, it is rare for condominium development to stop. </ref>.

* {{ill|Ten'an|Q1075611|qid=Q1075611|lt=Ten'an}} January 27, 3rd year ({{ill|859|Q23897|qid=Q23897}}), from the upper fifth rank to the lower junior fourth rank ("{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}") - Written as "Tarumi no Kami" <ref group="Hara" name="New Year's Day of the 1st year of Jogan">New Year's Day 27th, 1st year of Jogan (859) in "Nihon Sandai Jiroku" (Refer to {{Harvnb|Shinto and Shrine Historical Materials Collection}}). </ref>.

== Setsusha ==
The following shrines are enshrined as shrines within the precincts and shrines outside the precincts.
*Suesha
** Ebisu Shrine - Deities enshrined: Kanayamahiko no Mikoto, Kanayamahime no Mikoto, Toyoukehime no Mikoto, Kotosushi no Mikoto
** Haredo Shrine - Deities enshrined: Ibukito no Mikoto, Seoritsu Hime no Mikoto, Hasakai Tsu Hime no Mikoto, Hasasa Sura Hime no Mikoto
** Kotaisha - Deities enshrined: Isanaki no Mikoto, Isanami no Mikoto, Amaterasu Omikami
** Kusunosha Shrine - Deities enshrined: Owatatsumi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahimekami
* Otabisho
** Kusunoki Shrine - Enshrined deity: Owatatsumi no Mikoto, Ichikishimahime no Kami
* Others
** Fudosha

== Festival ==
The following festivals are held at Tarumi Shrine each year.
* Monthly Festival/Monthly Festival (1st and 15th of every month)
* Fudosha Goma (8th of every month)
* Saitan Festival (January 1st)
* Tarumi Ebisu (January 10th)
* Donto Festival (January 15th)
*Setsubun Festival (February 3rd)
* Yoimiya (Otabisho Festival) (May 20th)
* Spring Festival (May 21st)
* Summer Purification (June 30th)
* Yoimiya (Otabisho Festival) (October 20th)
* Autumn Festival (October 21st) - ``Regular Festival''.
* Great Purification (December 31st)
